sections.h2: Drilling takes Rs 43,200 crore, about half of the Rs 84,084 crore outlay

chart.title: Drilling and seismic data absorb most of the Rs 84,084 crore outlay
chart.sub: Components as reported, Rs crore, to 2030-31.

sections.means: The drilling line, not the seismic data, is the largest single claim on the money, although the components reported sum to Rs 350 crore less than the total.
sections.todo: Ask the ministry to publish what the Rs 350 crore unitemised line funds before the scheme's first awards.

sections.h2: The Rs 675 crore cap binds on any deepwater well above about $142 million

chart.title: Most quoted well costs sit at or below the $142 million point where the cap binds
chart.sub: Cost of one deepwater well, $ million.
chart.source: Petroleum minister, Sept 2026; Swarajya; Rs at 94.93 a dollar (23 Oct 2026), this blog's arithmetic.
ref: 142 = Rs 1,350 crore, where the cap binds

sections.means: At these costs the scheme pays close to half, turning a $100–145 million bet into a $50–75 million one for the drilling company.
sections.todo: Check whether the Rs 675 crore cap, reported as Rs 650 crore in some reports, is fixed in the released scheme text.

sections.h2: Only 21 of 172 OALP blocks have reported a discovery, and one produces

chart.title: The scheme's record so far: 21 discoveries and one producing field
chart.sub: Counts of OALP blocks and outcomes since 2017.
chart.source: DGH figures to March 2026, as reported in this blog's OALP piece.

sections.means: The deepwater record shows discoveries are not the bottleneck; the trouble came after discovery, in development and output.
sections.todo: Judge the scheme by production from its finds, not only by wells drilled and reserves added, as the post argues.
